searchText: Just implemented the mergeNetsplitBlock for Sepolia, resulting in ForkID: `0xb96cbd13` <@&688101493978562687> <@&652918665943056397> <@&836981603216654336> Can you guys confirm this pls? Confirmed 🙂 Added this in the PR as well 🙂 Given that Geth + Nethermind confirmed here + Erigon approved the PR, once Besu 👍's I'll merge it 🙂 confirmed. are we not calling this the parisBlock though? fyi in the besu PR (https://github.com/hyperledger/besu/pull/4158/files#diff-1b538af227412f8532d769e86e1c92ea103ca5e35c2a834b2428b3fc38876643R16-R17) I added terminalBlockNumber and terminalBlockHash as well. Consensus clients might complain about a config mismatch. At some point we should do this. The net split block seems like the right time to do this? <dannyryan> Why add terminal block hash? That is a config var to dictate the merge rather than to set post facto. I would suspect clients will complain and tbh support is not universal I believe. <dannyryan> And the merge split block is not Paris, it's a p2p upgrade after Paris so I wouldn't suggest conflating the name Yeah I think this is the wrong thing to do. It's fine to embed the terminalBlockNumber and terminalBlockHash into the client as an optimisation but that's not the same as setting the override terminal number and hash and shouldn't be used in the engine_exchangeConfiguration response or we'll have to teach users to ignore the big scary warnings that were put there deliberately to tell them about a misconfiguration and shouldn't be ignored. yeah my understand of what the post-merge fork consisted of must be dated. knowing the terminal block hash when syncing could be useful, but forkId_next serves the same purpose. Removed. I can definitely see that knowing the terminal block hash could be useful, it's just a different value to the terminal block hash *override* which is a user specified config option. There's no reason you couldn't track both if its helpful, just need to keep them separate enough to return the right thing in engine_exchangeConfiguration

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> Why add terminal block hash? That is a config var to dictate the merge rather than to set post facto. I would suspect clients will complain and tbh support is not universal I believe.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> And the merge split block is not Paris, it's a p2p upgrade after Paris so I wouldn't suggest conflating the name

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: Yeah I think this is the wrong thing to do. It's fine to embed the terminalBlockNumber and terminalBlockHash into the client as an optimisation but that's not the same as setting the override terminal number and hash and shouldn't be used in the engine_exchangeConfiguration response or we'll have to teach users to ignore the big scary warnings that were put there deliberately to tell them about a misconfiguration and shouldn't be ignored.

excerpts.author: suburbandad_
excerpts.content:
yeah my understand of what the post-merge fork consisted of must be dated.  

knowing the terminal block hash when syncing could be useful, but forkId_next serves the same purpose.  Removed.

excerpts.content: I can definitely see that knowing the terminal block hash could be useful, it's just a different value to the terminal block hash *override* which is a user specified config option.  There's no reason you couldn't track both if its helpful, just need to keep them separate enough to return the right thing in engine_exchangeConfiguration
